about: Born, Not Made, simplified version after the sketch of 21 November 2026. Frame: x toward the opening, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor (the tank floor is 3 mm lower).

stages.name: Dock
stages.text: The tail docks to the gel chamber: three disc magnets on the thin docking ring pull onto three steel discs.

stages.name: Unfold, gel
stages.text: The arm unfolds and injects the gel: 3.0 L at 0.5 L per minute.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The suction cup picks the electronics kit once and places the kit in the gel, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change at the rack: suction cup off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release).

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the folded newborn around the kit: 40 m of bead, 0.08 L of Dragon Skin 10 NV.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, pneumatic module on.

stages.name: Air in, nose up
stages.text: The nozzle enters the valve. Air pushes the trapped gel out of the folds, the newborn floats up in the gel, and the arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the lip.

stages.name: Push while inflating
stages.text: The arm steers the tail end from above and pushes; the newborn slides over the lip, and each segment opens outside. No contractions.

stages.name: Hold and fill
stages.text: The arm holds, the newborn fills to full size, the nozzle lets go.

stages.name: Float
stages.text: The newborn floats in the water: gravity, buoyancy, drag, a damped settling.

stages.name: Swim
stages.text: The newborn takes ballast, sits lower and swims on two jets.

notes: The tail is set down behind the gel chamber and slid forward on the tank floor; three magnets close the last millimeters.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, over the gel wall. The base does not move.
Gel comes through the line on the arm; the arm moves the outlet over three fill points.
The bare arm goes to the pneumatic module, which waits with the cup on the kit.
The quick release clicks onto the module.
Vacuum on: the cup holds the kit.
The kit is carried over the gel.
The kit goes straight down through the gel onto the three seat bumps.
Vacuum off: the kit stays on the seat, the cup lifts clear.
Tool change: the pneumatic module goes back into the fork.
The pin on the fork presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm crosses to the print needle.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle goes over the kit.
The folded newborn is printed around the kit, layer by layer, in clear silicone.
The silicone cures in the gel (75 minutes at room temperature). The print needle goes back to the rack.
The pneumatic module is back on the arm: the same nozzle that held the kit now carries the air.
The nozzle goes to the valve on the tail end of the newborn.
Air at 450 Pa pushes the gel out of the folds through the vent in the nose; the drained newborn rises 30 mm and floats in the gel.
The nozzle presses the tail end down in the gel: the nose rises above the lip of the opening.
Push while inflating: every segment opens once the segment is out of the opening. All the air comes through the nozzle on the arm.
At full reach the arm holds the nozzle in the valve while the rest of the air goes in; the skin stretches by a quarter and the creases pull smooth.
The nozzle lets go. The newborn floats free, rocks and settles; the arm parks the module and folds back into the tail.
The kit pumps take water into the belly pocket until the jets are under water; the newborn swims a slow turn on two jets.

pairs.name: arm and tool, rack, shelf and seat
kit, hull, rack and parked module

checks.name: Tail prints in one piece on the H2S: 336 x 314 x 336 mm of 340 x 320 x 340
Gel chamber prints in one piece: 287 x 314 x 336 mm
Folded arm ends 18 mm behind the docking face; tower top 14 mm under the tail roof

A tool rack in the tail: at the docking face the wrist is at most 129 mm above the floor, the print needle tip 7 mm, the gel wall 114 mm. Tools cannot cross from the tail, so the rack and the kit shelf sit in the gel chamber, above the gel
The print needle reaches all 1140 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges
The tail rests on the floor in 88 mm of water: weight 7.2 kg (gel moved out), buoyancy 6.4 kg
The filled gel chamber rests on the floor: weight 4.4 kg, buoyancy 2.4 kg
The empty gel chamber alone would float (1.4 kg against 2.4 kg of buoyancy): the docked tail holds the gel chamber down, the three magnets carry 48 N in shear at friction 0.3 against the 10 N needed
The lip of the opening is 31 mm above the water and 12 mm above the gel; the docking seam starts 29 mm above the water
Gel volume 3.02 L; the bags in the tail hold 3.04 L

Battery, air pump box, controller, gel pump and silicone cartridge fit behind the arm in the one piece tail; the gel bags do not fit there and sit beside the arm (deepest overlap with the shell 0.1 mm)
Every pose of the timeline is inside the official joint ranges (base -21 to 21, J1 0 to 57, J2 2 to 85 degrees)
Suction: the 15 mm cup holds 3.7 N (35 kPa, 60 percent seal), the kit weighs 1.05 N: margin 3.5
Payload while carrying the kit: 167 g of 500 g
Force of the nozzle on the valve stays under the payload: peak 2.33 N of 4.91 N
The olive on the nozzle holds the largest upward pull on the valve: 1.37 N of about 2 N (estimate, to bench test)
The newborn leaves through the center of the opening
checks.value: the axis passes 55 mm below the center: the body rides on the lip, on the centerline

checks.name: Folds can be printed: story pitch 5.0 mm with one valley, pleat walls 7.1 mm apart at mid depth (limit: 1.2 mm wall plus 2 mm of gel)
Kresling stories are bistable with a barrier strain of 3.1 percent, far under the 25 percent stretch of the skin
Stretch 1.25 stays under the limit point of the membrane (1.38) and uses 4 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
Full size 395 x 280 mm against the gel chamber 287 x 314 x 336 mm: 138 percent of the length, 89 percent of the width
The newborn floats upright: metacentric height 34 mm dry, 76 mm with ballast
Draft 28 mm dry; 0.45 kg of water in the belly pocket puts the jets 45 mm under water
The motion settles: pitch rate in the last three seconds under 0.18 degrees per second; deepest contact at the lip 0.00 mm
Per frame penetration test over 2004 frames: deepest overlap of any pair 0.00 mm (limit 1 mm)
UNS 120S: the parent body (623 mm long, 336 mm tall) and the newborn (395 mm) fit in the 1176 mm inner length; water 51 L, about 122 kg filled

deriv.name: Arm base
deriv.value: 115 mm behind the docking face, on the tail floor
deriv.why: The folded DexArm reaches 97 mm ahead of its axis; the axis sits as far forward as the folded arm allows, so the reach into the gel chamber is the largest possible: the tool tip gets 277 mm past the docking face at the height of the print.

deriv.name: Tail
deriv.why: The folded arm stands 314 mm tall on a 2 mm pad; the roof is 14 mm above the tower. The equipment zone behind the arm is 135 mm deep. One print on the H2S (340 x 320 x 340 mm), docking face down, 4, 6 and 4 mm clear of the build volume.

deriv.name: Print needle
deriv.why: The head stays above the gel (92 mm deep over the lowest printed point) while the tip prints the lowest layer.

deriv.name: Printed newborn
deriv.why: With the needle hanging 122 mm below the wrist, the arm reaches from 94 mm to 277 mm past the docking face at the axis of the print, and from 124 mm to 253 mm at its top. The 150 mm body lies from 106 mm to 256 mm. The 90 mm diameter is the smallest that holds the kit on the belly.

deriv.name: Full size newborn
deriv.why: The skin that packs into the folded volume at the packing of the full size study (silicone 47 percent of the folded volume): 0.173 m2. Kresling stories (n = 16, twist 22.6 degrees a story) open the length, sixteen star pleats open the girth, a 25 percent stretch pulls the creases smooth. Unfolding at about 300 Pa (estimate), full at 1344 Pa.

deriv.name: Tail end of the newborn
deriv.value: a neck of 40 mm radius for the first 129 mm
deriv.why: At full reach the valve is 74 mm short of the lip. The part of the body still inside must pass the opening while the nozzle holds the valve, so the first three stories stay narrow: the newborn has a tail as well.

deriv.name: Gel
deriv.why: The gel covers the 90 mm print by 5 mm. The lower lobe of the gel chamber is narrowed to 114 mm across at the axis of the print, and the keel rises to the docking face, so the shell itself holds the gel and little gel is wasted.

deriv.name: Docking face
deriv.value: open above 114 mm, a thin 4 mm ring, three magnets
deriv.why: The keel of both parts rises to 114 mm at the docking plane: above the gel (104 mm) and above the water (85 mm). The seam is dry and needs no seal. Three DC2-N52 disc magnets on steel discs hold 161 N.

deriv.name: Rack and kit shelf
deriv.value: in the gel chamber, 257 mm from the arm axis, 21 degrees to each side
deriv.why: At the docking face the wrist of the DexArm is at most 129 mm above the floor. The print needle hangs 122 mm below the wrist, so its tip would cross the 114 mm gel wall at 7 mm: no tool and no kit can be carried from the tail into the gel chamber. Where the wrist is high enough to hold the tools clear of the gel, the tip is 257 mm from the axis, which is inside the gel chamber. The modules hang in two forks; the pneumatic module waits with its cup on the kit, so the kit needs no pick up move.

deriv.name: Opening
deriv.value: lip at x 284 mm, z 116 mm; 202 x 241 mm; face leaning back 20 degrees
deriv.why: The lip is 12 mm above the gel and 31 mm above the water. The lip is as close to the arm as the print allows, because the nozzle reaches only x 210 mm at the height of the valve (the limit there is 219 mm). The lower half passes the newborn; the upper half gives the module head room at full reach.

deriv.name: Gel chamber
deriv.why: Length from the reach of the arm (the lip), width from the rack and the kit shelf at 21 degrees, height from the arm passing the docking face. One print on the H2S, docking face down, 53, 6 and 4 mm clear.

deriv.name: Water
deriv.why: Deep enough for the newborn with ballast (draft 45 mm) with 43 mm under the belly; low enough to stay 31 mm under the lip and 29 mm under the docking seam.

deriv.name: Time
deriv.why: Gel 6 min at 0.5 L per minute, print 39 min for 40 m of bead at 20 mm per second, cure 75 min, air 57 s for 11.3 L at 12 L per minute.

deriv.name: Printing the two parts
deriv.why: Tail: 336 x 314 x 336 mm in print orientation, about 1.7 kg of clear PETG at a 3 mm wall, about 20 h at 18 mm3 per second. Gel chamber: 287 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.4 kg, about 17 h. Both stand on the docking face, so the domes close without tall supports; the rack forks and the kit shelf need supports that break off. The fallback is not needed: each part in two blocks, split on the horizontal plane at half height, with a 6 mm tongue and groove and a solvent weld.

verdict.point: Two printed parts, tail and gel chamber, each in one piece on the H2S
verdict.why: Tail 336 x 314 x 336 mm, gel chamber 287 x 314 x 336 mm, against 340 x 320 x 340 mm.

verdict.point: Docking face with magnets, thin ring
verdict.why: Three disc magnets, 161 N; the ring is 4 mm; the seam is 29 mm above the water.

verdict.point: The shell of the gel chamber holds the gel in its lower part
verdict.why: 3.02 L, surface at 104 mm, held by the keel that rises to 114 mm at the docking face.

verdict.point: DexArm on a fixed base in the tail, no boom, no rail; folds back, unfolds to work
verdict.why: Axis 115 mm behind the docking face; the folded arm ends 18 mm behind the face; all 2004 poses of the timeline are inside the joint ranges.

verdict.point: The arm as drawn: a tower, then two long links over the top of the docking face
verdict.why: The tower of the DexArm already contains the upper arm: the shoulder is 127 mm above the base and each link is 150 mm. The wrist reaches 279 mm above the floor at most, and only close to the base; at the far end of the print the wrist is at 208 mm.

verdict.point: One opening, on a slant at the upper front, thin plain rim, no magnets
verdict.ok: yes, lower and less slanted than drawn
verdict.why: The lip is at 116 mm, as low as the gel allows, and the face leans back 20 degrees. The nozzle on the fixed arm reaches 176 mm high at x 210 mm and no further, so the opening has to come to the arm.

verdict.point: Equipment behind the arm in the tail
verdict.ok: yes for battery, controller, air pump, gel pump and silicone; the gel bags sit beside the arm
verdict.why: About 5 L are free behind the arm in the 340 mm print; the rigid parts take 3.1 L and the gel 3.0 L, so the gel goes into four soft bags beside the arm.

verdict.point: Tool modules and the kit store in the tail
verdict.why: At the docking face the wrist is 129 mm above the floor at most; the print needle tip would pass at 7 mm, under the 114 mm gel wall. The rack and the kit shelf sit in the gel chamber, above the gel, where the wrist is high.

verdict.point: The parent body rests on the tank floor; only the newborn floats
verdict.why: In 88 mm of water the tail weighs 7.2 kg against 6.4 kg of buoyancy, the filled gel chamber 4.4 kg against 2.4 kg; the empty gel chamber is held down by the docked tail.

verdict.point: The newborn grows to about the size of the gel chamber
verdict.why: Printed 150 x 90 mm, full size 395 x 280 mm: 138 percent of the length and 89 percent of the width of the gel chamber, 63 percent of the length of the whole parent body. The limit is the skin that packs into a print the arm can reach.

verdict.point: Birth by pushing while inflating, all air through the arm
verdict.why: The nozzle steers the tail end from above; the body slides over the lip; peak force 2.33 N of 4.91 N. A vertical tool cannot pull the body up a ramp, so the gel carries the body inside and the lip and the water carry the body outside.

limits: Estimates, to measure: the mass of the DexArm (2.4 kg), the size of the Air Pump Box, the module head (30 x 40 x 52 mm), the vacuum of the pump (35 kPa) and the seal of the cup, the pressure that opens the folds (300 Pa), the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), the pump curve of the kit pumps, friction at the lip (0.2).

How the official joint angles J1 and J2 map onto the link meshes is an assumption, as on the full version. The DexArm specification page could not be opened again from here on 21 November 2026; its numbers are those used on the full version.

The valve is a soft boss on the tail cap and the nozzle stays vertical while the body pitches by up to 39 degrees: this needs a bench test. So does the drain of the gel from the folds, and whether a fold packed this tightly prints and opens as drawn.
The force on the valve is a quasi static estimate from slices: weight, buoyancy in the gel and in the water, the lip with friction, yield drag.

The newborn is drawn rigid with one soft droop where the body leaves the opening; a real skin at 300 Pa also wrinkles. In the force estimate the unfolded part outside is limp at that droop: the lip, the hull front and the water carry that part, and the arm steers only the part still inside. Friction at the gel wet lip is taken as 0.2.
The 0.45 m of open water in this tank lets the newborn swim only a short run and a slow turn.
Overlap is measured from sampled points (4 to 11 mm apart) against exact surfaces, so a figure can be about 1 mm off.

read.birth_text: Quasi static estimate from slices. Peak 2.33 N; the payload of the DexArm is 4.91 N. The nozzle pushes forward and down; the gel carries the body inside, the lip and the water carry the body outside.
read.tank_text: The tank is the Ultum Nature Systems UNS 120S, a rimless low iron glass tank of 1200 x 600 x 360 mm with 12 mm glass (259 L to the brim). The parent body, 623 mm long and 336 mm tall, stands on the floor at one end; 88 mm of water (51 L) leave the lip of the opening 31 mm above the water and give the newborn 492 mm of open water ahead. Filled as shown the tank weighs about 122 kg.
